Prevention: Rotate cotton every two years with maize, beans, cabbage, millet, cassava or other vegetables.
Uproot and burn crop residues as soon as possible after harvest.
Ensure that the fields are free from weeds as some weeds harbour aphids.
Avoid application of broad spectrum pesticides (i.e. abamectin) to preserve natural enemies such as lady bird beetles and parasitic wasps, which assist in reducing pest populations.
Monitoring: Check plants in the field once a week for the presence of aphid nymphs.
Cotton aphids are 1-3mm long, soft- bodied insects with long antennae and 2 projections at the rear.
They vary in colour from yellow to yellow/green to very dark green/black.
Aphids on the underside of young leaves cause curling of the leaves and also look for boll shedding and stunting of the plant.

Direct Control: When infestation is light or at an early stage, apply soapy water.
Tablet soap or liquid soap can be mixed with water and applied using a knapsack sprayer.
Add nimbecidine to water not water to nimbecidine and stir well.
If plants are severely affected, they can be uprooted and burned.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
